newsitem.title: USA: Case says profits jump 25 percent.
newsitem.headline: Case says profits jump 25 percent.

text.p: Case Corp. said Thursday its earnings rose 25 percent in the second quarter, thanks to record sales of agricultural and construction equipment.
It earned $138 million, or $1.82 a share, up from profits of $110 million, or $1.47, in last year's second quarter.
Revenues rose 9 percent to a record $1.6 billion, from $1.4 billion.
"Recent acquisitions and solid retail demand supported sales growth in the quarter, particularly in higher margin equipment," said Jean-Pierre Rosso, chairman, president and chief executive officer.
"We also benefited from additional cost reduction actions that will contribute to future earnings," he said.

In North America, second-quarter sales of Case's major agricultural equipment were down from a year earlier, as heavy overseas shipments of some products constricted availability in North America, the company said.
In Europe, sales of Case agricultural equipment were up 25 percent.
Case said North American construction equipment sales jumped to the highest level since 1990.
Case's stock was off 44 cents at $65.50 on the New York Stock Exchange.
